name: Country Lane Memory Care Assisted Living

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the interior baffles of the ice machines had an accumulation of soil residues. CORRECTED: PIC stated that the ice machines had just been cleaned that morning. Inspector confirmed that the ice machine had just been cleaned, as there was very little ice in the machine. PIC immediately contacted the facility’s maintenance person, who arrived quickly and removed the ice machine from service to clean and sanitize the interior of the ice machine during the inspection. Inspector observed that the ice machine interior was now clean, and discussed with staff better methods of monitoring the hard-to-reach area (using a mobile phone camera and a flashlight). Ensure that food-contact surfaces are kept clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the following must be cleaned: (1) The upper portion of the ice machine (not in contact with the ice); and (2) The ceiling vent over the hand washing sink. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the ice machine and ceiling vent are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces need to be cleaned: (1) The soil on the coffee machine upper portion that is in contact with the coffee pot; (2) The food debris on the top of the microwave; and (3) The debris on the floor in the dry storage area underneath the shelves along the back wall. All non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced areas are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived. An employee made up a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. The inspector educated about the importance of sanitizer buckets. Ensure there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
A bag of cooked ground beef was observed without any date marking in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC referred to the menu, determined that the ground beef was prepared yesterday, and labeled it accordingly. Ensure foods are labeled with the date prepared, and are used or discarded within 7 days of that date.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
A mop was observed sitting in dirty water in a mop bucket on arrival to the facility. The mop was removed from the bucket and bucket was dumped. Corrected on site. Ensure that mop buckets are emptied immediately after cleaning floors and are hung in the top of the mop bucket or inverted against the wall when not in use to allow air drying and preventing contamination.

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Both single door cooling units are observed to be holding food at above 41F. The unit next to the ice machine is holding food at 43F to 45F and the unit closest to the walk in cooler is holding food between 45F and 48F. The external and internal thermometers are reading above 50F in both units. The PIC was either not aware or believed that it was acceptable for the temperature to be in this range. It was explained to the person in charge that food shall not be above 41F even if the unit doors are open and shut a lot or the unit is in a defrost cycle. 

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in both of the single door reach in coolers are above 41F. The foods were discarded except for a few items which were not labeled refrigerate after opening or had for quality statements in their labeling. Foods in the unit close to the stove were mostly cooked items that had been made in house.  Items in the unit next to the ice machine were mostly bottled sauces and condiments. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Two single door cooling units are not functioning properly. The internal thermometers read above 50F and the units both have water in the bottoms of them. Call when repairs are made so that the units can verified as functioning. 

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Observed a wet wiping cloth to be on the counter near food preparation activities. Store wet wiping cloth in sanitizer when not actively being used. Cloth was placed into the soiled cloth bag.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed at least two rubber spatulas that have cracks in the rubber blades. Discard and replace these items as wear and tear dictate.  

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Worker was observed going between tasks without a glove change. The same gloves were worn to place dirty dishes in the dish machine for a ware washing cycle, touch the handle of a reach-in cooler door, scoop ice into a pitcher at the ice machine, and turn on the cold water at the prep sink to fill the pitcher. Worker then returned to the dish machine to handle and put away clean dishes without first changing gloves. Proper glove use was discussed, and gloves were discarded to allow for a handwash prior to putting on a new pair of gloves. Ensure gloves are changed after touching general surfaces and prior to handling clean dishes or returning to food preparation. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was observed reading at 30F at room temperature. PIC noted the thermometer fell on the floor the evening prior and must have caused the dial to move. Thermometer was calibrated to 32F in an ice water solution. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometer was discussed. Educational handout on calibrating stem thermometer with ice water method was provided for future reference. (see general comments for additional information)
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.
